title: ChatGPT is poorly designed. So I fixed it
talk_summary: A UX critique of ChatGPT (voice and text siloed, model choice opaque) with a demo of a unified voice+text interface built on Realtime API and tool calls. The transferable engineering idea is heuristic-based model routing: cheap/fast model handles simple asks, and tool calls hand off to a reasoning model when the request is complex.

takeaways.technique: Heuristic complexity-based handoff to reasoning model
takeaways.what_they_do: The front model detects that a request is complex (e.g. 'refactor this entire codebase') and writes a plan with a reasoning model instead of attempting it directly; simple asks stay on the fast path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it detects that it's complex and decides to write a plan with the reasoning model to make sure the code actually works

takeaways.what_they_do: Routing decisions are made with simple heuristics on the user's phrasing rather than a learned router.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This is a really effective pattern that you can do with some heristics. If you asked for details and pros and cons

takeaways.technique: Tool calls as the channel for structured side-output
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a system prompt, a single tool with a good description ('send chat message') is used to route long-form content to a text panel while voice continues.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Didn't even need a system prompt. Just added this description and it was smartly able to send the right stuff with text.
